excitation.explanation: Excitation wavelength is the colour of the laser. Raman shift is the energy difference between the laser light and the scattered light, in cm-1, so the same vibration appears at the same shift for every excitation wavelength while the scattered light appears at different wavelengths. A spectrum cannot be 'recoloured' to another laser: fluorescence, detector response, resonance enhancement and noise change with excitation and need a new measurement.

data.distinction_note: An axis-calibration error moves the x coordinates of an unchanged signal; a physical change moves the signal on a fixed axis. In the reported coordinates the two can look the same; only metadata or a calibration standard can tell them apart. Nonlinear warping, broadening, baseline distortion and intensity scaling are different operations and are swept separately.

explanation.headline: Your spectrum looks most like the Paracetamol demo reference, but that reference is simulated, so this is not a real identification.

what_we_found.text: We found 10 peaks, the material's 'fingerprint'. The strongest sit at 1324, 1648, 1236 cm⁻¹.
This fingerprint lines up with Paracetamol with a similarity of 1.00 out of 1, clearly ahead of the next closest material, Polypropylene (0.13).
When we shifted the chart sideways by up to ±20 cm⁻¹ to mimic a calibration error, the best match stayed the same.

explanation.how_sure: Not applicable: the closest reference is simulated, so the result only shows how the software works.
what_this_does_not_mean: This is a research tool. It is not a certified, medical, legal or safety identification.
Only the 5 materials in the library can be recognised. A sample made of something else may still look closest to one of them.
A mixture of materials, a coating, or a container (glass, plastic bag) can change the fingerprint.
The similarity score describes how alike the shapes are; it is not the chance that the answer is right.
next_steps: Write down how the spectrum was measured (temperature, excitation wavelength, laser power…) so the result can be repeated.
Check the instrument's calibration with a silicon wafer in the same session: its peak should sit at 520.7 cm⁻¹.
Compare against measured reference spectra, not simulated ones.

glossary.plain: A chart of how a material scatters laser light. Each material gives its own pattern, like a fingerprint.
A spike in the chart. The positions of the peaks are what identify a material.
The unit on the chart's horizontal axis; it says where a peak sits.
How closely two fingerprints line up, from 0 (nothing alike) to 1 (identical shape). It is not a probability.
The collection of known materials the sample is compared with. Only materials in it can be recognised.
How clearly the peaks stand out from random fluctuation. Low values mean a noisy measurement.
The evidence was not strong enough to name a material, so the software declines to guess.
